g.data-label: The problem: People who ship Emscripten SINGLE_FILE builds pay about 33% base64 overhead plus an inline decoder, and gzip or brotli is the best compression they can get in a self-contained HTML file.
g.text: People shipping Emscripten SINGLE_FILE builds pay about 33% base64 overhead plus an inline
decoder, and gzip or brotli is the best compression they can get in a self-contained HTML file.

g.data-label: The evidence: a write-up on small, fast web builds, at zeux.io/2019/03/11/small-fast-web/.
g.text: A write-up on small, fast web builds: zeux.io/2019/03/11/small-fast-web/

g.data-label: Today's fix: Emscripten -sSINGLE_FILE with base64, or a gzip or brotli payload in base64 decoded with DecompressionStream.
g.text: Emscripten -sSINGLE_FILE (base64), or a gzip or brotli payload in base64, decoded with

g.data-label: The gain, on file size: on a 200 KB wasm-opt -Oz module, the HTML file comes out at least 15% smaller than a gzip-9, base64 and DecompressionStream file of the same module, and decodes in under 300 ms on a 2020 laptop.
g.text: Claim that a test can prove false: on a 200 KB wasm-opt -Oz module, the HTML file is at
least 15% smaller than a gzip-9 plus base64 plus DecompressionStream file of the same
module, and decodes in under 300 ms on a 2020 laptop.

g.data-label: What happened: the idea survived the hunt. The closest prior art is Roadroller, which handles JavaScript only, plus histos and wasm-squeeze, which use brotli or LZ. No tool was found that combines order search and context mixing for Wasm. The size gain is still unmeasured, and the decoder is slower.
g.text: Closest prior art: Roadroller (JavaScript only), histos and wasm-squeeze (brotli or LZ).
No tool found that combines order search and context mixing for Wasm. The size gain is
still unmeasured, and the decoder is slower.
